import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

**Task:** run work that a call cannot (minutes of CPU over large files that must stay private) and keep its result in your app.

This guide is the how-to.
Why a run is built the way it is, and every rule a node applies, is in the [Compute actions](/protocol/compute-actions/) chapter.
Every snippet is from `apps/compute-redact` (a CSV redactor) or `apps/v2-fixtures/compute`.

## A compute method or a normal method

A call stops at 2 s, and its whole log entry stays under 1 MiB.
A compute run may take up to 15 minutes, reads and writes sealed files, and leaves only a small result in the log.

- Use a normal method for anything that reads or writes state.
- Use a compute method for work that only turns files into files, such as redaction, transcoding or a digest.
- A compute run has no state, no network and no way to start another run.
  It reaches state in one place, its **result method**, which the node runs as an ordinary logged call when the run ends.

Compute runs need a component app (the `calimero-sdk` and `wasm32-wasip2` toolchain).

## Build the two components

A compute method is marked in the same crate as the rest of the app.
The crate is built twice, once as `app.wasm` (every method, the state, the result methods) and once as `compute.wasm` (the compute methods only, which is all a job node receives).

```bash
scripts/install-mero-app-build.sh
mero-app-build apps/compute-redact --out app.wasm --compute-out compute.wasm
```

Without `--compute-out`, the compute component is written beside `--out` as `compute.component.wasm`.
A crate with no compute method builds one component and no compute output.

Pack both into the signed bundle, which carries the compute component as `compute` next to `wasm`:

```bash
scripts/pack-component.py --wasm app.wasm --compute compute.wasm
```

A raw single `.wasm` upload has no compute component and cannot start runs, so ship the `.mpk`.
The install checks are in [Compute actions](/protocol/compute-actions/#two-components).

## Write a compute method and its result method

```rust
use calimero_sdk::compute::{self, ComputeOutcome, ComputeStatus};
use calimero_sdk::files;

#[app::compute(
    fuel = 100_000_000_000,
    memory_mib = 256,
    wall_secs = 300,
    result = "on_run"
)]
pub fn redact(policy: Policy, job: String, start: u32, rows: u32) -> app::Result<Redacted> {
    let reader = files::open(&input()?)?;
    let mut writer = files::create()?;
    // let stats = rules::redact_part(reader, &mut writer, ...), reporting compute::progress as it goes
    writer.finish()?;
    Ok(Redacted { rows: stats.rows, cells: stats.cells })
}

fn input() -> app::Result<BlobRef> {
    compute::inputs().into_iter().next().ok_or_else(|| Error::NoInput.into())
}
```

- `fuel`, `memory_mib`, `wall_secs` and `result` are the four attributes, and the caps cannot exceed the host's ([Limits](/protocol/limits/)).
  `result` names the result method.
- `compute::inputs()` lists the input files the run was started with, and `compute::progress(percent, step)` reports progress (it is never logged).
- `files::open` gives a `Read` and `files::create` a `Write`.
  `finish()` returns the output's `BlobRef`, and a writer dropped unfinished leaves no file.
- The return value is the run's `result`, at most 64 KiB.
- The run is deterministic: its clock is fixed and its randomness is seeded per run, so a retry writes the same bytes.

The result method takes the whole outcome:

```rust
#[app::compute_result]
pub fn on_done(&mut self, outcome: ComputeOutcome) -> app::Result<()> {
    if outcome.status == ComputeStatus::Done {
        for output in &outcome.outputs {
            self.kept.insert(&output.id.id(), &output.id)?;
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

- `outcome` has `run`, `method`, `attempt`, `status` (`Done`, `Failed` or `Cancelled`), `reason`, `result` (base64, only when done), `outputs` (`id`, `size`, `sha256`) and `usage`.
- **An output is kept only if the result method stores its `BlobRef`.**
  One it does not store is forgotten an hour after the run ends.
- The result method is not public: no client can call it, so no client can forge an outcome.
- If it fails, the run keeps its outcome but its outputs go the same way.

### Start the next run from a result method

A result method is a logged write, so it may call `compute::start`.
`compute-redact` does this: the `preview` run's result method plans the parts and queues them, and every result method starts waiting runs while fewer than 4 are active.

```rust
#[app::compute_result]
pub fn on_then(&mut self, outcome: ComputeOutcome) -> app::Result<()> {
    let started = match compute::start("digest", &(), &[]) {
        Ok(run) => run.to_string(),
        Err(e) => format!("error: {e:?}"),
    };
    self.chained.insert(&outcome.run.to_string(), &started)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

`start(method, &args, &inputs)` takes the arguments as anything serializable (`&()` sends none) and answers a `RunId`.
Each input must be one of the app's own sealed files.
A run with the same method, arguments and inputs that is still active is answered instead of a second one, so a retried call starts nothing twice.
A call may start at most 16 runs, and an app may have 64 active.
A refused start (for example when the release ships no compute component) returns an error you can handle, as `compute-redact` does by failing the job.

## Sealed files and who may submit

A sealed file is a blob whose bytes the app can read only inside a compute run.
A call or a view can ask a file's size and hash (`file.info()`), and `files::open` is refused there.
The bytes leave only as a compute output you publish.

A client uploads one through `/apps/{app}/files`: one request up to 16 MiB, else a session of parts that can be resumed.
Only the app's owner and members of its organization may upload, and the answer carries the file's `id`, which a call takes as a `BlobRef`.
`calimero-client`'s `Client::upload_file` picks between the two and resumes a dropped upload, and `meroctl file upload` runs it on a file.
`meroctl blob upload` uploads an ordinary blob, not a sealed file.

The app sets the policy for who may start a run.
`compute-redact` lets a member submit only a file they uploaded, and admins any file:

```rust
pub fn submit(&mut self, file: BlobRef, rows_per_part: Option<u32>) -> app::Result<String> {
    let who = member()?;
    if file.info().is_none() {
        return Err(Error::NoSuchFile.into());
    }
    if !is_admin() && files::uploader(&file).as_deref() != Some(&who) {
        return Err(Error::NotYourFile.into());
    }
    // ... store the job, queue its first run with compute::start ...
}
```

`files::uploader(&file)` is the account the node recorded from the authenticated upload.
It is `None` for a file a call or a run made, and cannot be called inside a compute run.

## Exporting a file

The node never hands out a sealed file's plaintext or its key in the clear.
`Client::export_file(app, id)` makes a fresh X25519 key pair for the call and asks `POST /apps/{app}/files/{id}/export { recipient }`.
The node answers the file's segment hashes and its data key wrapped to that public key, and serves each ciphertext segment at `GET /apps/{app}/files/{id}/segments/{k}`.
The client checks the segment list against the file id, each segment against its hash, then the plaintext size and SHA-256, and returns bytes only when all of it matches.
Only the app's owner and members of its organization may export, even on a public app, and one account gets `429 TOO_MANY_EXPORTS` past 30 exports a minute on a node.
`meroctl file download APP ID --out PATH` runs it on one file, and `meroctl pipeline download APP RUN [--out DIR]` on every output of every step of an ended run, as `STEP-INDEX.bin`.

## Pipeline run receipts

`GET /apps/{app}/pipeline-runs/{run}/receipt` answers `{ receipt, node, signature }` once the run has ended (`409 RUN_NOT_ENDED` before), for the app's owner and members of its organization.
The receipt names the cluster identity, release, pipeline hash, the compute component of each module, the inputs and params, and per step the status and, for each run, the job node, job key, assignment digest, the hash and signature of the job's report and the files it made; a run answered from the step cache is listed as `cached` with its cache key.
`signature` is the answering node's receipt key over `"calimero.pipeline.receipt.v1\0"` and the receipt's canonical JSON, and `Client::verify_receipt` checks it under the key `verify_app_cluster` attests.
`meroctl pipeline receipt APP RUN [--verify] [--out FILE]` prints it, and with `--verify` also downloads each output and compares its SHA-256 with the receipt.
It does not yet verify each job's report signature on the client (the node's signature vouches for them), and it carries no module logs.

## Start, list and cancel runs

There is no "start a run" route.
A run starts when a logged call, timer or `init` calls `compute::start`, so you expose it as an ordinary method and call that:

```bash
meroctl call -c CONTEXT submit --args '{"file":"<file id>","rowsPerPart":50000}'
```

`GET /apps/{app}/runs/{run}` answers one run's state, attempts, input and output ids, usage, reason and `progress` while it runs.
`GET /apps/{app}/runs?limit=<n>&before=<cursor>` lists the active runs and the last 256 finished ones, newest first.
Neither carries the arguments or any key.
They are reachable from `meroctl raw get` (the node API reference lists them).

To cancel, expose a method that calls `compute::cancel(&run)`, and decide in it who may:

```rust
pub fn cancel(&mut self, run: RunId) -> app::Result<()> {
    compute::cancel(&run)
}
```

The result method then receives a `Cancelled` outcome.
A run that already finished keeps its report and outputs.

## Share an output with a grant link

A sealed output cannot be downloaded or granted.
`compute::publish` turns the output of one of the app's done runs into a plain blob, in a logged write, and `grant` gives a link to it:

```rust
pub fn publish(&mut self, output: BlobRef) -> app::Result<BlobRef> {
    let blob = compute::publish(&output)?;
    self.published.insert(&blob.id(), &blob)?;
    Ok(blob)
}

pub fn link(&mut self, job: String, part: u32, ttl_secs: u32) -> app::Result<String> {
    // ... check the caller may see the job, find the published part ...
    Ok(part.grant(ttl_secs))
}
```

- Store the published blob's `BlobRef`, or it is forgotten like any unreferenced blob.
- A published output over 47 MiB cannot be published, so size parts below that.
- `grant(ttl_seconds)` takes 1 to 86,400 seconds and is a call, so the log records who shared it (a view is refused for a published blob).
- Anyone holding the grant downloads with `GET /apps/{app}/blobs/{id}?grant=<grant>`, with no session.
- The app's owner or an org admin ends every grant made so far with `meroctl blob revoke ID -c CONTEXT`, or removes the blob with `meroctl blob delete ID -c CONTEXT`.

## Test it before you deploy

Run the compute component alone with `mero-compute`:

```bash
scripts/install-mero-compute.sh
mero-compute run compute.wasm --method redact \
  --args @apps/compute-redact/example/redact.json \
  --input apps/compute-redact/example/people.csv \
  --out out --twice
```

It uses the engine, caps and determinism of a job node, writes outputs to `out/output-0` and fails, naming the reason, if a cap is hit or if `--twice` finds the two runs differ.
It runs no app, no state and no result method ([mero-compute](https://github.com/calimero-network/core/blob/master/tools/mero-compute/README.md)).

Test the app side with the SDK's `TestApp` harness, which runs the real component but no compute: `compute::start` fails on the host target.
`compute-redact` therefore passes the start and the publish as parameters (`Starter`, `Publisher`) and tests the queue and the outcomes with fakes in `src/lib.rs`.
`TestApp::add_run_output` seeds a file that `compute::publish` accepts.

## Limits and failures

The numbers are in [Limits](/protocol/limits/) and the chapter's [limits table](/protocol/compute-actions/#limits).
What to expect:

- A run has at most 3 attempts.
  A node that goes silent, or a wall clock that runs out, loses the attempt and the run restarts on another job node, then ends `failed` with reason `lost` when the attempts are spent.
- Running out of `fuel` or `memory` is the app's failure: the run ends `failed` at once with that reason, and no output is registered.
- Your result method sees every ending: `status` and `reason` tell it which.
  The reasons are listed in [One run's life](/protocol/compute-actions/#one-runs-life).
- A restart must give the same output, so keep the method a pure function of its inputs and arguments.
- A run no job node takes within 10 minutes ends `refused`, and one over the organization's quota waits in the queue.
  See [Restarts, cancel and caps](/protocol/compute-actions/#restarts-cancel-and-caps).

<Aside type="tip">
  Keep a part's output under 47 MiB and its progress step under 128 bytes, and split big files into one run per part, as `compute-redact` does.
</Aside>
